# Adjudication Task — Chapter 325

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃325화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|전율.
  6|
  7|그건 이 자리의 모두가 공유하는 감정이었다.
  8|
  9|화산, 개방, 종남, 하오문과 용봉표국까지. 잘게 떨리는 수십 쌍의 눈동자가 눈앞에 벌어진 광경을 아연히 바라보았다.
 10|
 11|“그러니까.”
 12|
 13|퍽!
 14|
 15|“좋게 말할 때.”
 16|
 17|퍽!
 18|
 19|“멈췄어야지.”
 20|
 21|퍽!
 22|
 23|“어디서 선빵을, 선검을 날려?”
 24|
 25|뻐억!
 26|
 27|마지막 타격음은 유난히도 컸다. 커억, 피가래 끓는 소리와 함께 노인의 신형이 털썩 쓰러졌다.
 28|
 29|온통 피범벅이 된 얼굴. 한때 숱한 여인들의 방심(芳心)을 흔들었던 날렵한 콧대는 풀썩 주저앉은 지 오래였고, 팔순 나이가 무색하던 고른 치아는 이제 앞니 하나밖에 남아 있지 않았다.
 30|
 31|“남의 사부를 가지고, 패드립을, 시발 거.”
 32|
 33|뻐억!
 34|
 35|마지막 앞니 하나가 허공을 훨훨 날아 다루 구석에 떨어졌다.
 36|
 37|망연자실한 얼굴로 그 광경을 바라보던 이들의 머릿속에 순간 한 가지 생각이 떠올랐다.
 38|
 39|‘내가 지금 뭘 보고 있는 거지?’
 40|
 41|일어나리라고 생각지 못했던, 아니 일어나서는 안 되는 일이 벌어지고 있었다.
 42|
 43|이제 막 강호에 이름을 알리기 시작한 약관 언저리의 청년이, 종남파 제일의 고수이자 장문인의 사형을 옴팡지게 두들겨 패고 있다면 어느 누가 믿을 것인가.
 44|
 45|그러나 이 자리에 있는 모두는 똑똑히 지켜보았다.
 46|
 47|감히 눈으로 좇을 수도 없었던 두 사람의 공방을. 그리고 공방 끝에 쓰러진 노인과 홀로 우뚝 선 청년을.
 48|
 49|“화룡(火龍)…….”
 50|
 51|누군가가 신음처럼 중얼거린 그 두 글자가 사람들의 가슴을 깊이 파고들었다.
 52|
 53|산서잠룡. 그것이 지금껏 무림에 알려진 청년, 진태경의 무명(武名)이었다.
 54|
 55|하지만 틀렸다. 잠룡은 마침내 몸을 일으켰고, 산서가 아닌 천하의 창공을 누빌 것이다.
 56|
 57|한 마리의 화룡이 되어.
 58|
 59|“내가 살면서 유일하게 백 점 맞아 봤던 과목이 도덕이었는데, 오늘만큼은 노인 공격 제대로 한다. 일어나.”
 60|
 61|아니, 화룡이 아니라 광룡(狂龍)이었나?
 62|
 63|그을음과 핏물로 엉망이 된 황보엄의 수염을 머리채인 양 휘어잡는 진태경의 모습에, 완전히 넋이 나가 있던 서른 명의 태을검대는 정신이 번쩍 들었다.
 64|
 65|노인이 누구인가. 사문의 존장(尊丈)이자 장문인의 사형인 태을무정검 황보엄 아니던가.
 66|
 67|“자, 잠깐!”
 68|
 69|“사조님!”
 70|
 71|약속이라도 한 듯 동시다발적으로 터져 나오는 목소리.
 72|
 73|그 가운데에 유난히 우렁차고 강한 힘이 실린 외침이 있었다.
 74|
 75|“놈! 사백님을 놓아드리지 못할까!”
 76|
 77|태을검대를 이끄는 대주이자 종남파의 이대 제자인 황천(黃泉)이 황급히 검을 뽑으며 앞으로 나선 그 순간이었다.
 78|
 79|스르릉, 철컥.
 80|
 81|“……!”
 82|
 83|황천의 눈이 접시처럼 팽창했다.
 84|
 85|그것은 그야말로 찰나에 벌어진 일이었다.
 86|
 87|그의 목젖에서 멈춘 서늘한 검날. 싯누런 죽장(竹杖)은 가슴을 짚고 있었고, 검집을 반쯤 빠져나왔던 검신은 누군가의 검에 걸려 더는 나오지 못하고 있었다.
 88|
 89|절정 고수인 황천을 순식간에 제압한 세 남녀가 차례대로 입을 열었다.
 90|
 91|“그 검, 뽑지 않는 게 좋을 거요.”
 92|
 93|“싸움을 원하신다면 저와 용봉표국이 상대해 드리지요.”
 94|
 95|“타구봉법으로 맞으면 제법 아플 거다. 아직 오 성까지밖에 못 익혔지만.”
 96|
 97|화산일학 백무성, 은비화 주화란, 그리고 개방의 후개 궁기방까지.
 98|
 99|그뿐만이 아니었다.
100|
101|“소국주를 지켜라!”
102|
103|“곤란해. 이제 다 끝나 가는데 이대로면 곤란하지.”
104|
105|총표두 허준과 뜻 모를 말을 중얼거리던 냉막한 인상의 송일섬이 용봉표국의 표사들을 이끌고 종남파의 제자들과 대치했고…….
106|
107|“개방의 거지새끼들에게 분타주가 명한다. 저 황구(黃狗)만도 못한 놈들에게 개몽둥이 맛을 보여 줘라!”
108|
109|“같은 거지면서 새끼가 뭡니까.”
110|
111|“어이구, 간만에 살풀이 한번 거하게 하겠구나.”
112|
113|“조금이라도 다치면 분타주 책임이오. 구걸 못 한다고 구박이나 하지 마시오.”
114|
115|흑걸개와 개방의 방도들이 허리춤에 매단 몽둥이를 기세 좋게 꺼내 들었으며.
116|
117|“너희들은 괜히 끼어들어서 다치지 말고 모든 상황을 빠짐없이 적으렴. 나중에 비싸게 팔 수 있을 테니까.”
118|
119|“저어, 종남파를 적으로 돌리실 셈입니까?”
120|
121|“응? 중요한 고객을 왜 적으로 돌리니. 이거 종남파에 팔 건데. 엄청 올려쳐도 살 수밖에 없을걸?”
122|
123|“아아, 역시!”
124|
125|“그림도 그려. 당장이라도 튀어나올 것처럼 생생하게.”
126|
127|“옙!”
128|
129|크게 한탕을 노리는 월화와 하오문 문도들은 눈앞의 광경을 빠짐없이 글과 그림으로 옮기기 시작했다.
130|
131|“우와! 살면서 이런 상황 처음이에요!”
132|
133|“이놈들! 대태원진가의 진룡대 부대주이자 조장님의 오른팔인 이 혁무진도 있다!”
134|
135|마지막으로 한 발자국 떨어져서 강 건너 불구경하던 청풍과 혁무진까지.
136|
137|일이 뜻하지 않게 흐르자 황천의 얼굴이 당황과 분노로 붉게 물들었다.
138|
139|“이, 이게 무슨! 모두 당장 멈추시오!”
140|
141|대답은 다른 곳에서 나왔다.
142|
143|“멈추기 싫다면?”
144|
145|“……!”
146|
147|황천은 숨을 들이켰다.
148|
149|종남파의 앞을 가로막은 사람들의 어깨 너머, 차가운 불꽃이 일렁이는 한 사람의 눈동자가 그를 응시하고 있었다.
150|
151|“내가 물었잖아. 멈추기 싫으면 뭐 어쩔 거냐고.”
152|
153|빈정거리는 진태경의 입가에서 새하얀 김이 뿜어져 나왔다.
154|
155|믿지 못할 신위(神威)을 목도해서일까? 시선을 마주하고 귓가를 파고드는 나직한 목소리만으로도 숨이 턱 막혔다.
156|
157|기세. 그것은 실로 압도적인 기세였다.
158|
159|‘이, 이토록 젊은 나이에 어찌.’
160|
161|황천은 다시 한번 깨달았다. 종남 제일의 고수를 쓰러트린 저 청년에게 있어 나이는 숫자에 불과하다는 것을.
162|
163|‘괴물, 저자는 괴물이다.’
164|
165|그리고 지금, 바로 그 괴물이 자신을 바라보고 있다.
166|
167|뛰어나다 자부했던 무공이 이처럼 하잘것없이 느껴질 줄이야. 진태경의 기세에 압도된 황천이 연신 마른침을 삼키던 그때였다.
168|
169|“사제, 이만 물러나거라. 다른 분들도 검을 거두시오.”
170|
171|가라앉은 목소리와 함께 눈앞을 가로막는 한 사람의 등.
172|
173|익숙한 뒷모습에 황천이 눈을 부릅떴다.
174|
175|“혁 사형……!”
176|
177|종남일룡 혁소평. 종남파의 미래라 불렸고, 주색에 빠진 지금도 그 명성을 잃지 않은 종남 최고의 후기지수.
178|
179|황천의 앞에 선 그가 굳은 눈빛으로 진태경을 응시했다.
180|
181|수십 개의 병장기가 겨누고 있음에도 한 치의 흔들림 없는 음성이 흘러나온다.
182|
183|“의미 없는 싸움을 멈춰 주시오.”
184|
185|“의미가 없어? 멈춰 줘?”
186|
187|피식, 진태경의 입술 사이로 바람 빠지는 소리가 흘러나왔다.
188|
189|“시작은 너희가 했어도 끝내는 건 나야.”
190|
191|“알고 있소. 그래서 부탁드리는 거요.”
192|
193|“부탁이라. 주둥이 뚫렸다고 말 함부로 하는 거 아니다. 그러다가 진짜 뚫리는 수가 있거든.”
194|
195|“이미 승패는 명백한 바, 강자의 아량을 베풀어 주시길 청하는 거요.”
196|
197|놀랄 만큼 정중한 그의 태도며 음성보다도, 그 말이 담은 내용에 종남파의 제자들은 눈을 부릅떴다.
198|
199|그의 뒤에서 잠시 침묵을 지키고 있던 황천이 고개를 쳐들며 외쳤다.
200|
201|“사형! 강자의 아량이라니요, 그 말씀은 사백님과 대종남파의 위신을 떨어트리는…….”
202|
203|“사제.”
204|
205|“예, 예?”
206|
207|황천의 말을 끊어 낸 목소리는 부드러웠으나, 이어지는 말은 서슬 퍼런 칼날과 같았다.
208|
209|“그 입 닥치지 못하겠느냐.”
210|
211|“……사형?”
212|
213|황천뿐만 아니라 태을검대의 모두가 얼빠진 표정으로 혁소평을 바라보았다.
214|
215|혁소평은 그런 사제들의 시선을 한 몸에 받으며 천천히 입을 열었다.
216|
217|“맹인(盲人)이 아니었다면 보았을 것이다. 또한 농인(聾人)이 아니었다면 들었을 것이다. 이 모든 일이 어떻게 시작되었는지.”
218|
219|“…….”
220|
221|“음지에서 용봉표국을 집어삼킬 계략을 꾸몄으니 이는 당당한 명문 대파의 처사가 아니다. 하여 본문은 이미 위엄(威嚴)을 잃었다.”
222|
223|목소리는 가라앉았고 표정은 일그러져 있었다. 그러나 혁소평은 말을 멈추지 않았다.
224|
225|“또한 이토록 명백한 증거 앞에서 과오를 인정하지는 못할망정 살심을 품고 검을 휘둘렀으니, 이는 본문에 남아 있던 한 줄기 신망마저 끊어진 것이다. 한데 우리 중 누가 감히 위신을 입에 담는다는 말이냐. 본분을 잊고 주색에 빠져 허우적대던 나? 아니면 잘못을 인정하지 않고 자존심만 지키려는 너희?”
226|
227|황천은 고개를 푹 숙였다. 비단 그뿐만이 아닌 서른 명의 종남파 제자들 모두가 입을 다물고 허리춤에 걸린 검갑을 으스러져라 움켜쥐었다.
228|
229|그들은 혁소평의 입에서 흘러나온 말들이 사실이라는 것에 부끄러움을 느꼈고, 뼛속 깊이 스며들어 있는 사문에 대한 자부심이 허물어짐에 허탈함과 치욕감을 느꼈다.
230|
231|아무도 입을 열지 않았지만, 그들이 느끼는 감정만큼은 생생하게 주위에 전해졌다.
232|
233|“적어도 오늘만큼은…… 우린 대종남파가 아니었다.”
234|
235|마지막 한마디.
236|
237|회한 어린 눈빛으로 사제들을 바라보던 혁소평이 몸을 돌렸다. 그리고 아무 말 없이 자신의 말을 끝까지 기다려 준 한 사람을 향해 깊숙이 포권지례를 취했다.
238|
239|“종남 제자 혁소평이 감히 청합니다. 본문이 저지른 잘못을 깊이 반성하고 사과드리니, 부디 이번 한 번만 아량을 베풀어 그를 살려 주십시오.”
240|
241|마치 무림의 전대 고수를 대하듯 지극히 공손한 태도.
242|
243|그러나 포권을 받은 상대방은 새파랗게 어린 청년이었다.
244|
245|잠시 후, 고개 숙인 혁소평을 물끄러미 바라보던 진태경의 입술이 열렸다.
246|
247|“이런 개 같은 노인네를 살려 두기에는 입맛이 영 껄끄럽긴 한데…… 좋아, 한 번만 봐주지.”
248|
249|혁소평이 고개를 들기도 전에, 경쾌한 목소리가 이어졌다.
250|
251|“마지막 한 대만 더 때리고.”
252|
253|빠악!
254|
255|
256|
257|* * *
258|
259|
260|
261|다루 내부는 망가졌다는 말로도 부족했다.
262|
263|폭삭 내려앉은 지붕, 온갖 집기들은 나와 황보엄이 벌인 싸움의 여파로 가루가 되었고, 무너진 벽면에서는 찬바람과 함께 사람들의 웅성거림이 흘러 들어왔다.
264|
265|“세상에, 등왕루가…….”
266|
267|“이게 도대체 무슨 일이야? 어찌 된 일인지 아는 사람 없나?”
268|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Output contract

Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown fence or prose:

Reasons must name the veto, or say that SOL keeps sense and voice. Do not merely say one version is "better" or "more natural" without stating what changed.

Keep reasons brief. Do not adjudicate unchanged passages. Do not call tools.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 325

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃325화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|전율.
  6|
  7|그건 이 자리의 모두가 공유하는 감정이었다.
  8|
  9|화산, 개방, 종남, 하오문과 용봉표국까지. 잘게 떨리는 수십 쌍의 눈동자가 눈앞에 벌어진 광경을 아연히 바라보았다.
 10|
 11|“그러니까.”
 12|
 13|퍽!
 14|
 15|“좋게 말할 때.”
 16|
 17|퍽!
 18|
 19|“멈췄어야지.”
 20|
 21|퍽!
 22|
 23|“어디서 선빵을, 선검을 날려?”
 24|
 25|뻐억!
 26|
 27|마지막 타격음은 유난히도 컸다. 커억, 피가래 끓는 소리와 함께 노인의 신형이 털썩 쓰러졌다.
 28|
 29|온통 피범벅이 된 얼굴. 한때 숱한 여인들의 방심(芳心)을 흔들었던 날렵한 콧대는 풀썩 주저앉은 지 오래였고, 팔순 나이가 무색하던 고른 치아는 이제 앞니 하나밖에 남아 있지 않았다.
 30|
 31|“남의 사부를 가지고, 패드립을, 시발 거.”
 32|
 33|뻐억!
 34|
 35|마지막 앞니 하나가 허공을 훨훨 날아 다루 구석에 떨어졌다.
 36|
 37|망연자실한 얼굴로 그 광경을 바라보던 이들의 머릿속에 순간 한 가지 생각이 떠올랐다.
 38|
 39|‘내가 지금 뭘 보고 있는 거지?’
 40|
 41|일어나리라고 생각지 못했던, 아니 일어나서는 안 되는 일이 벌어지고 있었다.
 42|
 43|이제 막 강호에 이름을 알리기 시작한 약관 언저리의 청년이, 종남파 제일의 고수이자 장문인의 사형을 옴팡지게 두들겨 패고 있다면 어느 누가 믿을 것인가.
 44|
 45|그러나 이 자리에 있는 모두는 똑똑히 지켜보았다.
 46|
 47|감히 눈으로 좇을 수도 없었던 두 사람의 공방을. 그리고 공방 끝에 쓰러진 노인과 홀로 우뚝 선 청년을.
 48|
 49|“화룡(火龍)…….”
 50|
 51|누군가가 신음처럼 중얼거린 그 두 글자가 사람들의 가슴을 깊이 파고들었다.
 52|
 53|산서잠룡. 그것이 지금껏 무림에 알려진 청년, 진태경의 무명(武名)이었다.
 54|
 55|하지만 틀렸다. 잠룡은 마침내 몸을 일으켰고, 산서가 아닌 천하의 창공을 누빌 것이다.
 56|
 57|한 마리의 화룡이 되어.
 58|
 59|“내가 살면서 유일하게 백 점 맞아 봤던 과목이 도덕이었는데, 오늘만큼은 노인 공격 제대로 한다. 일어나.”
 60|
 61|아니, 화룡이 아니라 광룡(狂龍)이었나?
 62|
 63|그을음과 핏물로 엉망이 된 황보엄의 수염을 머리채인 양 휘어잡는 진태경의 모습에, 완전히 넋이 나가 있던 서른 명의 태을검대는 정신이 번쩍 들었다.
 64|
 65|노인이 누구인가. 사문의 존장(尊丈)이자 장문인의 사형인 태을무정검 황보엄 아니던가.
 66|
 67|“자, 잠깐!”
 68|
 69|“사조님!”
 70|
 71|약속이라도 한 듯 동시다발적으로 터져 나오는 목소리.
 72|
 73|그 가운데에 유난히 우렁차고 강한 힘이 실린 외침이 있었다.
 74|
 75|“놈! 사백님을 놓아드리지 못할까!”
 76|
 77|태을검대를 이끄는 대주이자 종남파의 이대 제자인 황천(黃泉)이 황급히 검을 뽑으며 앞으로 나선 그 순간이었다.
 78|
 79|스르릉, 철컥.
 80|
 81|“……!”
 82|
 83|황천의 눈이 접시처럼 팽창했다.
 84|
 85|그것은 그야말로 찰나에 벌어진 일이었다.
 86|
 87|그의 목젖에서 멈춘 서늘한 검날. 싯누런 죽장(竹杖)은 가슴을 짚고 있었고, 검집을 반쯤 빠져나왔던 검신은 누군가의 검에 걸려 더는 나오지 못하고 있었다.
 88|
 89|절정 고수인 황천을 순식간에 제압한 세 남녀가 차례대로 입을 열었다.
 90|
 91|“그 검, 뽑지 않는 게 좋을 거요.”
 92|
 93|“싸움을 원하신다면 저와 용봉표국이 상대해 드리지요.”
 94|
 95|“타구봉법으로 맞으면 제법 아플 거다. 아직 오 성까지밖에 못 익혔지만.”
 96|
 97|화산일학 백무성, 은비화 주화란, 그리고 개방의 후개 궁기방까지.
 98|

White steam billowed from Jin Taekyung’s sneering lips.

[P80]

[P81]
His aura was truly overwhelming.

[P82]
*H-how can someone so young…?*

[P83]
Hwangcheon realized it once again.

[P84]
To the young man who had defeated the Zhongnan Sect’s greatest master, age was nothing more than a number.

[P85]
*He’s a monster. That man is a monster.*

[P86]
And now that monster was looking directly at him.

[P87]
How could the martial arts he had once taken such pride in feel so insignificant?

[P88]
Hwangcheon swallowed dryly again and again as Jin Taekyung’s aura pressed down on him.

[P89]
That was when—

[P90]
“Junior Brother, withdraw. Everyone else, lower your weapons.”

[P91]
A calm voice sounded as a man stepped in front of him.

[P92]
Hwangcheon’s eyes widened at the familiar back.

[P93]
“Senior Brother Hyuk…!”

[P94]
Zhongnan One Dragon Hyuk Sopyung.

[P95]
He had been called the future of the Zhongnan Sect, and even now, despite his indulgence in wine and women, he had not lost his reputation as the sect’s greatest young prodigy.

[P96]
Standing before Hwangcheon, he stared at Jin Taekyung with firm eyes.

[P97]
Though dozens of weapons were pointed at him, his voice did not waver in the slightest.

[P98]
“Please end this pointless fight.”

[P99]
“Pointless? End it?”

[P100]
A short, breathy laugh escaped Jin Taekyung’s lips.

[P101]
“You might have started it, but I’m the one who decides how it ends.”

[P102]
“I know. That is why I’m asking.”

[P103]
“Asking? Just because you have a mouth doesn’t mean you can say whatever you want. Keep running it and someone might put a hole through it.”

[P104]
“The outcome is already clear. I ask you to show the mercy of the strong.”

[P105]
The Zhongnan disciples’ eyes widened—not at his surprisingly courteous manner or voice, but at the meaning of his words.

[P106]
Hwangcheon, who had remained silent behind Hyuk Sopyung, raised his head and shouted.

[P107]
“Senior Brother! The mercy of the strong? Those words dishonor Senior Martial Uncle and the Great Zhongnan Sect—”

[P108]
“Junior Brother.”

[P109]
“Y-yes?”

[P110]
Hyuk Sopyung cut him off in a gentle voice.

[P111]
But his next words were as sharp as a drawn blade.

[P112]
“Will you shut that mouth of yours?”

[P113]
“……Senior Brother?”

[P114]
Not only Hwangcheon, but all thirty members of the Taeeul Sword Unit stared at Hyuk Sopyung with blank expressions.

[P115]
Under the stunned gazes of all his junior disciples, Hyuk Sopyung slowly began to speak.

[P116]
“Anyone who wasn’t blind would have seen it. Anyone who wasn’t deaf would have heard it—how all of this began.”

[P117]
“…….”

[P118]
“We plotted in the shadows to swallow the Yongbong Escort Bureau whole. That is not the conduct of a great and prestigious sect. Therefore, our sect has already lost its dignity.”

[P119]
His voice was low, and his expression was twisted with pain. But Hyuk Sopyung did not stop.

[P120]
“Worse, even in the face of such clear evidence, we refused to admit our wrongdoing, harbored murderous intent, and swung our swords. That severed the last shred of trust our sect still possessed. And yet which one of us dares speak of reputation? Me, who forgot my duty and wallowed in wine and women? Or you, who refuse to admit your mistakes and cling only to your pride?”

[P121]
Hwangcheon lowered his head.

[P122]
He was not the only one. All thirty Zhongnan disciples fell silent, gripping the scabbards at their waists as if they meant to crush them.

[P123]
They were ashamed because everything Hyuk Sopyung had said was true. And as the pride in their sect that had seeped into their very bones crumbled, they felt devastated and humiliated.

[P124]
No one spoke, but everyone around them could feel those emotions.

[P125]
“At least today… we were not the Great Zhongnan Sect.”

[P126]
With those final words, Hyuk Sopyung looked at his junior disciples with eyes filled with regret, then turned around.

[P127]
He gave a deep fist-and-palm salute to the one man who had silently waited for him to finish.

[P128]
“This Zhongnan disciple, Hyuk Sopyung, humbly asks this of you. We deeply regret and apologize for the wrongs our sect has committed. Please show mercy just this once and spare him.”

[P129]
His manner was exceedingly respectful, as though he were addressing a revered master of the previous generation.

[P130]
And yet the person receiving his salute was a young man barely into his twenties.

[P131]
After staring silently at the bowed Hyuk Sopyung for a moment, Jin Taekyung opened his mouth.

[P132]
“It leaves a bad taste in my mouth to keep an old bastard like this alive… but fine. I’ll let him off this once.”

[P133]
Before Hyuk Sopyung could even raise his head, Jin Taekyung continued brightly.

[P134]
“After I hit him one more time.”

[P135]
Craack!

[P137]
The inside of Tengwang Pavilion was beyond ruined.

[P138]
The roof had collapsed completely, and all the furnishings had been reduced to rubble and dust by the battle between Hwangbo Eom and me. Cold wind and the murmuring of onlookers drifted in through the collapsed walls.

[P139]
“My heavens, Tengwang Pavilion…”

[P140]
“What on earth happened? Does anyone know?”

[P141]
“I don’t know the details either. But from what I’ve heard, about one shichen ago, Taeeul Merciless Sword of the Zhongnan Sect led his disciples…”

[P142]
Xi’an was the center of Shaanxi Province. No matter how far out of the way Tengwang Pavilion was, it could not escape the people’s attention.

[P143]
And the commoners who had gathered out of equal parts curiosity and concern found themselves facing dozens of sharp martial artists’ gazes.

[P144]
“That’s far enough.”

[P145]
“This is a matter of the martial world. Don’t get involved. Go back!”

[P146]
Dozens of armed martial artists formed a human wall to block their approach. The commoners hesitated, then slowly backed away.

[P147]
I clicked my tongue as I watched the Zhongnan disciples struggling desperately to keep the scene inside from being exposed.

[P148]
“Look at you trying so hard.”

[P149]
The Great Zhongnan Sect’s reputation was already shot to hell, yet they were still fighting to preserve even a shred of it.

[P150]
It was both pathetic and fucking stupid.

[P151]
I dropped into a wooden chair with a broken back and spoke.

[P152]
“Well, some unfortunate things happened, but we still have to finish what needs finishing. Let’s find some common ground through dialogue instead of barbaric violence.”

[P153]
“…….”

[P154]
“…….”

[P155]
Oof. Those stares were sharp.

[P156]
I ignored the gazes raining down on me from every direction and smiled at one person.

[P157]
“So, Great Hero Hwangbo, what do you think?”

[P158]
Hwangbo Eom answered immediately.

[P159]
Or rather, he groaned.

[P160]
“Hrrgh… hrrrgh…”

[P161]
Both of his arms were broken, and one leg was fractured. On top of that, he had suffered internal injuries that would require at least a year of recovery, while his nose and teeth had been smashed to pieces.

[P162]
A sobbing groan escaped from his slightly open mouth, accompanied by the wet rattle of blood and phlegm.

[P163]
“Hrrrgh…”

[P164]
I grabbed Hwangbo Eom by the wrist.

[P165]
Resisting the urge to break it, I sent a small amount of internal energy into him. A little color returned to his pale face.

[P166]
“Patient? Sir, wake up. It’s time for your injection—no, your negotiation.”

[P167]
“Hrrgh… Jin Taekyung. You…”

[P168]
“That catchphrase went out of fashion fifty years ago.”

[P169]
“You bastard. Do you really think our sect will let you get away with this…?”

[P170]
“Hm.”

[P171]
*What do I do? He still doesn’t seem to have come to his senses.*

[P172]
I scratched the back of my head, then whipped my hand out like lightning.

[P173]
Smack!

[P174]
“Guh!”

[P175]
Hwangbo Eom’s eyes rolled back from the slap.

[P176]
As he trembled all over and began to slide out of the chair, Hyuk Sopyung caught him and sighed.

[P177]
“Whew.”

[P178]
“It’s not my fault. He keeps begging for a beating. He’s practically demanding that I kill him. What else am I supposed to do?”

[P179]
“Even so, restrain yourself. Any more than this could endanger his life.”

[P180]
“You’ve had a rough time too. Judging by his personality, I can’t imagine he treated you particularly well either. Am I wrong?”

[P181]
“……What kind of person he was to me is irrelevant. He is my Master’s senior martial brother and a disciple of our sect.”

[P182]
The complicated expression on Hyuk Sopyung’s face suggested that there was some story between them.

[P183]
*He seems surprisingly decent now… Was that why he got drunk and caused all that trouble?*

[P184]
The question crossed my mind for an instant, but I had no intention of asking.

[P185]
I wasn’t particularly curious, either.

[P186]
There was something more important to deal with now.

[P187]
“All right, then. Let’s negotiate. Young Lady Ju, are you ready?”

[P188]
“Pardon? Y-yes, yes.”

[P189]
“You may state your demands.”

[P190]
*What on earth happened here? Is this a dream?*

[P191]
Still looking as though she could not quite believe what was happening, Ju Hwaran rubbed her flushed cheek and began to speak.

[P192]
“As compensation for this incident, the Yongbong Escort Bureau demands that the Zhongnan Sect void the contract and pay the contractual penalty—”

[P193]
Hwangbo Eom’s hoarse voice cut her off.

[P194]
“We refuse. Our sect will not pay any compensation.”

[P195]
I knew it.

[P196]
I gave the rigid Ju Hwaran a look.

[P197]
“Young Lady Ju, wait a moment.”

[P198]
“Yes?”

[P199]
“It’ll only take a second.”

[P200]
Without hesitation, I slapped Hwangbo Eom across the face.

[P201]
Smack!

[P202]
“Guh!”

[P203]
“Senior Martial Uncle!”

[P204]
“I’ll ask again. Are you paying compensation or not?”

[P205]
Hwangbo Eom glared at me with burning eyes.

[P206]
“Our sect will… not pay any compen—”

[P207]
Smack!

[P208]
“Guh! No compensation whatso—”

[P209]
Smack!

[P210]
“Guhhh! We’ll pay any compensation!”

[P211]
“Okay, compensation! Okay! Thank you!”

[P212]
Negotiation sure was easy.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
